final_answer:
In a quiet forest lived a tortoise named Theo, who was known for his slow but steady pace. While others admired his patience, Theo longed for something more—flight. He watched birds soar above the trees and dreamed of gliding through the sky. Safe

One day, a wise old owl named Orin noticed Theo’s longing. "You wish to fly?" he asked. Theo nodded, and Orin offered to teach him. "But flight requires more than desire—it needs strength, balance, and courage," he warned. Theo, eager to learn, began his lessons. Safe

Days turned into weeks as Theo practiced, stretching his legs and flapping makeshift wings. He fell many times, scraping his shell and bruising his pride. Yet he never gave up. Finally, one morning, he leapt from a hill and soared—briefly—before crashing into a patch of thorns. Safe

Though he had flown, Theo realized the joy was fleeting. He returned to his forest, where he could move at his own pace, and found contentment in his unique path. The moral of the story is: embrace your natural strengths, for forcing change may lead to temporary triumph but not lasting happiness. Safe
